evidence.methodology_note: Ecosystem Toolchain/Developer Ecosystem Maturity metrics scored against a frozen 5-component, 20-point rubric per metric, applied identically to all 10 languages across shards. This shard reports only the Kotlin score and its supporting raw evidence; other language shards report their own languages under the same rubric.

metric.core_tooling_availability_quality.limitations: Kotlin's newer 'Kotlin Toolchain' unified CLI/build tool is explicitly Alpha, so it was not scored as a mature core tool; scoring instead credits the long-mature Gradle/Maven/kotlinc/IntelliJ stack that constitutes the de facto core tooling used by the overwhelming majority of Kotlin projects today.

raw_findings.citation: <cite index="9-3,9-4,9-5">Download the latest version (kotlin-compiler-2.4.20.zip) from GitHub Releases. Unzip the standalone compiler into a directory and optionally add the kotlinc/bin directory to the system path. The bin directory contains the scripts needed to compile and run Kotlin on Windows, macOS, and Linux.</cite> <cite index="3-3">Also, you could use package managers, such as Homebrew, SDKMAN!, and Snap package.</cite>
raw_findings.finding: Kotlin's official CLI compiler is distributed via GitHub Releases and can also be installed through system package managers.

raw_findings.citation: <cite index="3-1">JetBrains provides official Kotlin IDE support for IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, and Visual Studio Code.</cite> <cite index="3-4,3-5">For IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio, the Kotlin plugin is bundled with each release. When the new Kotlin version is released, these tools will suggest updating Kotlin to the latest version automatically.</cite>
raw_findings.finding: JetBrains, Kotlin's creator, provides official first-class IDE support across multiple products.

raw_findings.citation: <cite index="15-1,15-2">Maven is a build system that helps manage Kotlin-only or mixed Kotlin−Java projects and automate your building process. It works with JVM-based projects and downloads required dependencies, compiles and packages your code.</cite> <cite index="2-9">The Kotlin Toolchain is still in Alpha and under active development.</cite>
raw_findings.finding: Kotlin has mature official Gradle and Maven integration, plus an emerging first-party 'Kotlin Toolchain' build tool still in Alpha.

raw_findings.citation: <cite index="19-2,19-3,19-4">detekt is a static code analysis tool for Kotlin that detects code smells, complexity issues, and potential bugs. This guide shows how to integrate popular tools like ktlint, detekt, SonarQube, SonarCloud, and Kover into your backend project for Maven or Gradle. ktlint is a Kotlin linter and formatter that enforces the official Kotlin coding conventions with no extra configuration.</cite> <cite index="26-7,26-8">detekt has 7,031 stars, ktlint 6,733, and Spotless 5,617, and all three were pushed to within the last 24 hours as of this writing (August 2026). All three are actively maintained, all three are free.</cite>
raw_findings.finding: Kotlin has widely-adopted static analysis/formatting tools (ktlint, detekt) and JetBrains documents their integration for Maven/Gradle projects; these are community rather than core-bundled tools.

raw_findings.citation: <cite index="8-8,8-9">The Kotlin 2.4.20 release is out! This release brings performance improvements, bug fixes, and tooling updates, and more.</cite> <cite index="4-3">In May 2024, JetBrains released Kotlin 2.0 featuring the new K2 compiler—a complete rewrite offering up to twice the compilation speed of its predecessor—as well as stabilised support for Kotlin Multiplatform.</cite>
raw_findings.finding: Kotlin has a frequent, predictable point-release cadence with continuous tooling updates and an active AI-tooling roadmap led by JetBrains.

rubric: 1. Official compiler/CLI availability, cross-platform packaging, and installability (0-20)
4. Auxiliary developer tooling: linter/formatter, static analysis, debugger (0-20)
5. Release cadence and active maintenance signal (0-20)

metric.package_dependency_management_qua.limitations: Kotlin does not have a single unified, mature package manager independent of the JVM build-tool ecosystem (unlike e.g. Cargo or npm as a single canonical tool); its package-management strength is substantially inherited from Gradle/Maven/Maven Central rather than being a Kotlin-native invention, and multiplatform-specific dependency/publishing tooling is documented as still maturing (legacy-mode deprecation warnings, Alpha-stage unified toolchain publishing).

raw_findings.citation: <cite index="16-1,16-2">Gradle is a popular build automation tool that is widely used in the Kotlin ecosystem. It offers a flexible and efficient way to manage dependencies, build scripts, and project configurations.</cite> <cite index="14-1,14-3">For your Kotlin Maven project, you can configure where Maven looks for artifacts beyond the default Maven Central repository and define the libraries your project depends on. By default, the mavenCentral repository is available for all Maven projects.</cite>
raw_findings.finding: Kotlin officially supports both Gradle (with a dedicated Kotlin DSL) and Maven as first-party build/dependency-management systems.

raw_findings.citation: <cite index="12-1,12-2">Adds a repository which looks in the Maven central repository for dependencies. The URL used to access this repository is {@value org.gradle.api.artifacts.ArtifactRepositoryContainer#MAVEN_CENTRAL_URL}.</cite>
raw_findings.finding: Kotlin dependency resolution defaults to Maven Central, giving it access to the entire mature JVM package ecosystem shared with Java/Scala/Groovy.

raw_findings.citation: <cite index="29-1">A single catalog centralizes all dependency coordinates, avoids version duplication, and lets every subproject share the same type-safe accessors.</cite> <cite index="36-3,36-4">To ensure consistent version alignment, a good approach is to use a version catalog to define dependency versions alongside a platform to enforce them. Use platforms when you need to influence or enforce version alignment across modules.</cite>
raw_findings.finding: Gradle (Kotlin's primary build tool) provides advanced resolution mechanisms including type-safe version catalogs and platform/BOM-based version alignment.

raw_findings.citation: <cite index="32-1,32-2">The dependency group:artifact:1.0 was published in the legacy mode. Support for such dependencies will be removed in the future.</cite> <cite index="2-3,2-9">Library publishing arrived in preview in 0.11, but only for JVM libraries. The Kotlin Toolchain is still in Alpha and under active development.</cite>
raw_findings.finding: Kotlin Multiplatform dependency management works through the Gradle plugin but is still evolving: legacy-mode multiplatform artifacts are being phased out with compatibility warnings, and the newer unified multiplatform library-publishing tool remains in preview/Alpha.

raw_findings.citation: <cite index="28-1">Open the gradle/libs.versions.toml file and add the kotlinx-datetime dependency to the version catalog</cite> <cite index="33-13">kotlin { //... sourceSets { commonMain { dependencies { implementation 'org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-core:1.11.0' } } } }</cite>
raw_findings.finding: JetBrains actively maintains a Kotlin-specific library ecosystem (kotlinx.* libraries) that is versioned and distributed through the same Maven Central infrastructure and integrated into multiplatform dependency workflows.

rubric: 1. Availability of mature, standard package managers (0-20)
2. Central repository scale, reliability, and shared JVM-ecosystem access (0-20)
3. Dependency-resolution feature richness (transitive resolution, version catalogs, conflict/version alignment) (0-20)
